'''Numan Yunusovich Satimov''' ({{langx|ru|Нуман Юнусович Сатимов}}) (15 December 1939 – 22 September 2006) was a [[USSR|Soviet]] and [[Uzbekistan|Uzbek]] [[mathematician]], [[Doktor nauk|Doktor Nauk in Physical and Mathematical Sciences]], [[academician]] of the [[Academy of Sciences of Uzbekistan]] (2000), and [[corresponding member]] of the [[Academy of Sciences of Uzbekistan|Academy of Sciences of UzSSR]] from 1979 to 2006, and a laureate of the Biruni State Prize (1985). He was a specialist in the theory of [[differential equation]]s, [[control theory]] and their applications.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://zbmath.org/authors/?q=ai:satimov.n-yu|title=Satimov, N. Yu|website=zbMath}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|title=Выдающиеся математики|last=Borodin|first=Alexey|last2=Bugay|first2=Arkadiy|publisher=Ряданьска Школа|year=1987|location=Kyiv|pages=461|language=ru|trans-title=Outstanding mathematicians}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.academy.uz/ru/academics/previous-members?page=9|title=Ранее состоявшиеся члены Академии Наук РУз|website=Academy of Science of the Republic of Uzbekistan|language=ru|access-date=October 1, 2019}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Satimov was born on 15 December 1939<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.mathnet.ru/rus/person18076|title=Персоналии: Сатимов Нуман Юнусович|publisher=www.mathnet.ru|language=ru|access-date=October 1, 2019}}</ref> in the city of [[Andijan]] in a working-class family.

In 1956, he was accepted to the [[Central Asian State University]] at the Faculty of Physics and Mathematics. In 1958, Satimov continued his studies at the [[Moscow State University|Moscow State University named after M. V. Lomonosov]] at the Faculty of Mechanics and Mathematics. After graduating from the university in 1962, he entered graduate school at the Uzbek Academy of Sciences' Romanovsky Institute<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.mathinst.uz/en|title=Uzbekistan Academy of Sciences V. I. Romanovsky Institute of Mathematics|access-date=October 3, 2019}}</ref> of Mathematics, where he worked as a junior research fellow from 1965 to 1968.<ref>{{Cite journal|date=2006|title=Академик Н. Ю. Сатимов|trans-title=Academician N. Yu. Satimov|url=https://drive.google.com/file/d/1q0QxE-LKzvlPL3Q8C2j4kgtvDmPz8GcU/view|journal=Узбекский Математический Журнал|language=ru|volume=10|pages=108}}</ref>

In 1968, under the guidance of Professor [[Vladimir Boltyansky|V. G. Boltyansky]], Satimov defended his thesis. In 1977, under the guidance of Professor E. F. Mischenko, he defended his doctoral dissertation (at the specialized council of [[Steklov Institute of Mathematics]]). In 1978, he was awarded the title of [[professor]]. In 1979, he became a [[corresponding member]] of the Academy of Sciences of the Uzbek SSR, in 2000 – academician of the [[Academy of Sciences of Uzbekistan|Academy of Sciences of the Republic of Uzbekistan]].

Since 1968, Satimov worked in [[Tashkent State University]]. In 1971, he became the head of a department at the Faculty of Applied Mathematics and Mechanics of [[National University of Uzbekistan|NUUz]]. From 1974 to 1976, Satimov worked as a senior research fellow at [[Steklov Institute of Mathematics]]. From 1985 to 1987 he served as the dean of the Faculty of Applied Mathematics and Mechanics. Since 2000, he was a leading researcher at the Uzbek Academy of Sciences' Romanovsky Institute of Mathematics.<ref>{{Cite journal|date=2006|title=Академик Н. Ю. Сатимов|trans-title=Academician N. Yu. Satimov|url=https://drive.google.com/file/d/1q0QxE-LKzvlPL3Q8C2j4kgtvDmPz8GcU/view|journal=Узбекский Математический Журнал|language=ru|volume=10|pages=108}}</ref>

Satimov died on 22 September 2006. He was buried at the Chagatai cemetery in Tashkent.

== Scientific interests ==
Satimov's primary research interest included the theory of differential equations, control theory and their applications. He founded the Tashkent Scientific School on the theory of controls and differential games. He led the research seminar “Optimal processes and differential games” for over 35 years.

Moreover, Satimov is the author of a textbook on differential equations and two monographs.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Методы решения задачи уклонения от встречи в математической теории управления|last=Satimov|first=Numan|last2=Rikhsiyev|first2=Badir|publisher="ФАН" АН РУз|year=2000|isbn=5-648-02716-8|editor-last=Azamov|editor-first=Abdulla|location=Tashkent|pages=176|language=ru|trans-title=Methods for solving the avoidance problem in mathematical control theory}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|title=Управляемые динамические системы и их приложения|last=Satimov|first=Numan|publisher=Tashkent State University|year=1987|location=Tashkent|pages=104|language=ru|trans-title=Managed Dynamic Systems and Their Applications}}</ref> He published more than 180 scientific papers; most of which have been translated and published in [[United States|US]] and [[United Kingdom|UK]] journals. Under his guidance, eight doctoral and more than twenty master's theses were prepared.<ref>{{Cite journal|date=2006|title=Академик Н. Ю. Сатимов|trans-title=Academician N. Yu. Satimov|url=https://drive.google.com/file/d/1q0QxE-LKzvlPL3Q8C2j4kgtvDmPz8GcU/view|journal=Узбекский Математический Журнал|language=ru|volume=10|pages=108}}</ref>

Since 1970, Satimov worked on a new section of the theory of controlled processes – the theory of differential [[pursuit–evasion]] games. He paid particular attention to the development of [[Lev Pontryagin|L. S. Pontryagin's]] methods. As a result, Satimov proposed and later developed the so-called third (modified) method for solving the problem of persecution.
